was the first Golden Globe Awards ceremony after the [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] (HFPA) disbanded in 2023. On June 12, 2023, the HFPA announced that all of its rights and properties related to the Golden Globes were acquired by [[Dick Clark Productions]] and [[Eldridge Industries]].{{cite web |url=https://goldenglobes.com/articles/dick-clark-productions-and-eldridge-acquire-golden-globes/ |title=Dick Clark Productions and Eldridge Acquire Golden Globes |publisher=[[Golden Globe Awards|Golden Globes]] |date=June 12, 2023 |access-date=December 3, 2023 |archive-date=December 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231201231335/https://goldenglobes.com/articles/dick-clark-productions-and-eldridge-acquire-golden-globes/ |url-status=live }} On February 21, 2023, the date of the ceremony was announced. It came back on a Sunday night slot after being moved to Tuesday for the previous year. On September 18, 2023, [[Glenn Weiss]] and [[Ricky Kirshner]] were announced as its executive producers and showrunners. On November 17, 2023, it was announced that [[CBS]] had acquired the broadcast rights to the ceremony, replacing the Golden Globes' long-time U.S. broadcast partner [[NBC]]. The nominations were announced on December 11, 2023, during an event co-hosted by [[Cedric the Entertainer]] and [[Wilmer Valderrama]].
